play.description: Playing maestro for the purple and gold, Luka Dončić showcased his elite court vision against the Nets. With the Lakers cruising in the second quarter at Barclays Center, Dončić threaded a perfect pass to a cutting Deandre Ayton who finished with authority. The Slovenian star dished out 5 assists while scoring 24 points in the Lakers' commanding 125-109 road victory on February 3, 2026.

Even when backed into a literal corner, Luka Dončić is savvy enough to find a way out. When the Dallas Mavericks’ four-time All-Star chased down a pass he had juggled in the corner, he was promptly met by a pair of Indiana Pacers defenders. With his back to the basket and few options at his disposal, Dončić surveyed the scene before leaving his feet and firing a bullet to the other side of the court into the waiting hands of an all-alone Jaden Hardy for a corner 3-pointer. Dončić scored a team-high 25 points while mixing in seven rebounds, six assists and zero turnovers to help Dallas prevail 127-104 on March 27, 2023.

When most players fall with the ball in their hands, the resulting play is a turnover. Luka Dončić isn’t most players. The three-time All-Star and All-NBA First Team selection loses his footing on a dribble against the New Orleans Pelicans and still has the wherewithal to improvise from the floor, threading the needle with a bounce pass through multiple defenders to hit Christian Wood for an easy slam. The do-it-all Dallas Mavericks star tallied 37 points, 11 rebounds, seven assists, two steals and a block in a Southwest Division showdown on October 25, 2022.

When Luka Dončić orchestrates in transition, defenses scramble and teammates feast - a reality the Utah Jazz learned firsthand. After creating one of his three steals in the second quarter, the Lakers' floor general pushed the pace, sent the ball through Kevin Love's legs to keep the play alive, and spotted Jaxson Hayes streaking toward the rim. Dončić lobbed a perfectly weighted pass that Hayes caught in stride and hammered home with a running alley-oop dunk, cutting Utah's lead to five. The Slovenian maestro finished with 33 points, 11 rebounds and 8 assists in the November 23, 2025 thriller.

Only time will tell, regarding the short and long-term winners of Luka Dončić’s blockbuster deal. As the Los Angeles Lakers prepared to trade leaguewide shock for the shockwaves and excitement coursing through its arena on February 10, 2025, though, it simply marked yet another deal that they couldn’t decline. As if running through the checklist of what truly makes a could-be icon in the purple-and-gold, Dončić —  in just 24 minutes — put tantalizing gifts on a brief showcase during a debut defined by versatility. Eager to shake off both Utah Jazz defenders and the rust from not playing since Christmas, Dončić’s redeeming bucket arrived in expected fashion, as he froze Walker Kessler just long enough to create the necessary space for a rhythm 3-pointer. One quarter later, in a sequence that one could say symbolized both “Luka Magic’s” arrival and paid tribute to past Laker legends at once, Dončić called dibs on a rebound before unleashing a length-of-the-court dime to his Hall of Fame-bound teammate, creating an easy score. Spurred on by 18,997 in support, Dončić’s Lake Show audition was a smash hit, as he recorded 14 points, five rebounds, four assists, a 3-pointer, and a +15 plus-minus.

Even at his controlled pace, Luka Dončić’s IQ and feel for the game guarantees that he’s always one step ahead of nearly any defense in his path. Unguardable in both the pick-and-roll and isolation, Dončić uses both to get an ideal matchup, allowing him to work a quick crossover, drawing a double team in the process. In a one-of-a-kind example of passing precision, the Dallas Mavericks superstar uncorks a pass just behind the head of one defender, and just out of reach of another, right into the hands of his teammate for a clutch 3-point bucket. Orchestrating a thrilling two-point win over the Los Angeles Lakers, Dončić’s final stat line on December 12, 2023 was just as awe-inspiring: 33 points, six rebounds, 17 assists, and three 3-pointers.

Celebrations, it’s said, are still a work in progress for Luka Dončić, as he continues stacking must-see moments in the Los Angeles Lakers’ purple-and-gold. In the meantime, California’s new generational talent can rest assured, knowing that he gave 18,997 in attendance plenty to cheer for during his first-ever clash against his former team. Doing his best to mask inevitable emotions — and any intentions on could-be passes — during his downhill drive, Dončić, catching sight of his backwards-drifting teammate out of his peripheral, proceeds as normal until reaching the heart of the paint. Putting even the in-game cameraman to work, the all-seeing superstar unleashes a no-look, over-the-head dime to a teammate, securing a 3-point assist in highlight fashion. As calm as a flowing river after picking up a technical just minutes in, Dončić cooled himself into a 19-point, 15-rebound, 12-assist triple-double, alongside three steals and two blocks, bringing tangible impact on both sides. Riding that wave, Los Angeles survived the Dallas Mavericks’ competitive efforts for a win on February 25, 2025, a victory that ultimately helped spark an eight-game winning streak.

As the minutes wound down prior to Game Two of the NBA Finals, Luka Dončić — taped like a mummy with wrap encircling both his knee and chest area — stood calmly as the trainers prepared him for his career's biggest game to date. By night’s end, that wouldn’t be the only kind of wraparound the game would offer. Engaged in a battle of wits against a Boston Celtics defense focused on turning him into a facilitator, the Most Valuable Player Award finalist puts Jrue Holiday and Kristaps Porzingis through a pick-and-roll puzzle, almost magnet-like with both following his drive down the left baseline. In a brilliant show of court awareness, chemistry, and raw passing ability, Dončić unloads a no-look dime around Porzingis’ frame, back in the opposite direction and squarely into the hands of his teammate to set up a run-stopping 3-pointer. Battling through an assortment of injuries that left him questionable to play, the Dallas Mavericks superstar was a sure thing, even in defeat. In earning the 10th triple-double of his postseason career, Dončić stuffed the statsheet with 32 points, 11 rebounds, 11 assists, four steals, and four triples on June 9, 2024.

When Luka Dončić sets out with his mind set on scoring, there isn’t a defensive scheme capable of getting into his way. Dribbling down court with just five seconds remaining, Dončić moves through an obstacle course of Golden State Warriors defenders with behind-the-backs and spins before easing into his shooting motion to calmly drain a 32-foot triple to beat the buzzer. In their first Western Conference Finals appearance since 2011, Dončić put on a show for the Dallas Mavericks home crowd, finishing with 40 points, 11 rebounds, four triples, three assists and two blocks on May 22, 2022.

No matter the city, matchup or scenario, you can pencil in Luka Dončić as a guaranteed bucket. Hanging back in transition, the Dallas Mavericks star shows off his shooting touch in the All-Star Game, calmly draining a catch-and-shoot triple in traffic. Dončić chipped in eight points, three rebounds and two triples in Team LeBron’s 163-160 win on February 20, 2022.

When Luka Dončić surveys the court, his preternatural vision turns routine possessions into highlight-reel magic. With the Lakers pushing in transition during the first quarter, the Slovenian maestro tracked Jake LaRavia sprinting up the floor and threaded a one-handed bounce pass through traffic. LaRavia rose up to flush home the running alley-oop, cutting the deficit to 28-25 with 3:43 remaining in the opening frame. Dončić finished with a monster statline - 45 points, 14 assists, 11 rebounds - that has only been replicating once in NBA History.

Pick your poison when guarding Luka Dončić — let him score or hope the open teammate he finds misfires. The Denver Nuggets choose the latter option and are still left shaking their heads. The Dallas Mavericks superstar begins the possession looking for his own shot before his drive into the lane is met by a double team, so Dončić flicks a beauty of a no-look dish into the corner for an all-alone Christian Wood to bury the three-pointer. In yet another dominant performance, the three-time All-Star and All-NBA First Team selection tallied 33 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists — making him the second-fastest player to record 50 triple-doubles in his squad’s 127-99 win on November 18, 2022.

It’s one thing to have eyes on the back of your head, something else entirely to attempt the passes Luka Dončić attempts on a nightly basis. Charged with the task of picking apart a half-court defense, the Dallas Mavericks guard navigates to the top of the key, distracts a scrambling defense with a fake behind-the-back pass, then floats a no-look, kick-out pass over his own head right to teammate Maxi Kleber for an open triple. Dončić finished the January 29, 2022 contest with 30 points, six rebounds and 12 dimes.

A three-time All-Star and All-NBA First Team selection all by the age of 23 — somehow Luka Dončić still has higher to climb to reach his ceiling. Though that prospect may be hard to believe, the Brooklyn Nets got the full experience on October 27, 2022. Dončić reminds everybody that he can score every which way, from step-back triples to impossible-to-defend dribble drives that result in easy layups and floaters. The fifth-year star also remains an elite facilitator, as he nonchalantly sets up his teammates with a plethora of highlight-reel passes: an over-the-head no-look dish to Maxi Kleber, a spin-turned-kickout to Tim Hardaway Jr. and a behind-the-back dropoff to Reggie Bullock. When the final horn sounded, the Dallas Mavericks walked off with a 129-125 overtime road victory thanks to 41 points, 11 rebounds, 14 assists and three steals from Dončić, becoming just the 10th player in NBA history to record three 40-point triple-doubles.

Nature and animal-based TV networks could create full-length documentaries out of Luka Dončić’s predator-like hunt for fruitful matchups through pick-and-rolls, and given the postseason’s possession-by-possession style, it was only a matter of time before a reacquainting with Rudy Gobert would arrive. Eager to test his isolation chops against the four-time Defensive Player of the Year once more, Dončić brings the Minnesota Timberwolves’ star to the dancefloor, first working a series of between-the-leg dribbles to carve out a left-side driving lane. Donning his trademark smile before a shot attempt even goes airborne, Dončić finishes the sequence patiently, freezing Gobert with a pump fake before rainbowing home a soft-touch floater. Through a strong Game Two response, the Los Angeles Lakers ensured that Dončić’s dominant individual performance went accompanied by a series-tying performance on April 22, 2025. Becoming just the third-ever playoff Laker to produce back-to-back 30-point opens, Dončić’s final box score included 31 points, 12 rebounds, nine assists, one block, and two 3-pointers.

As evening arrived on March 31, 2024, and the Houston Rockets prepared to bring their 11-game win streak into a Texas-style dust-up against the Dallas Mavericks — on a six-game tear of their own —  it wouldn’t be long before Houston found that no moment was too big for Luka Dončić. Unfortunately for them, it also meant the town wouldn’t be big enough for the both of them. Seemingly poised to gift-wrap a bucket for every defender on Houston’s payroll, Dončić flips the switch to “trick-shot mode,” with Dallas ahead by 23. Calm in his aura, even with Jabari Smith Jr. playing his quick-twitch handle expertly and the play clock dwindling, Dončić pump-fakes before almost floating inside the 3-point arc, balancing into a one-legged, 21-foot-away finger roll, evoking an audibly-frustrated groan from the stunned road crowd. For most players, a 22-point, eight-rebound, four-assist performance represents a solid day’s work; for Dončić, it was merely his first quarter tally. In a showcase that upped the volume on his Most Valuable Player case tenfold, Dončić —  without even needing to play much in the fourth —  dazzled with 47 points, 12 rebounds, seven assists, two steals, and nine 3-pointers, lassoing in a win along the way.

Stepback 3-pointers over an aggressive double team? Check. One-handed, off-the-backboard shots against heavy defense from 25 feet away? You got it. Built for any challenge a defensive scheme can think to send his way, Luka Dončić certainly wasn’t one to waste time, giving the crowd —  and the Brooklyn Nets’ defense —  all they could ask for with four, jaw-dropping 3-pointers over a three-minute span, flipping the Dallas Mavericks’ once-sizable fourth quarter deficit into an unforgettable win on October 27, 2023. Every superlative in the book, Dončić’s numbers were equally breathtaking in the Mavs’ home opener: 49 points (on just 25 shots), 10 rebounds, seven assists, nine 3-pointers, and zero turnovers.

Give Luka Dončić an inch of daylight, and he'll make you pay from anywhere on the court. The Lakers' maestro worked his magic against Sacramento, losing his footing on the right wing before recovering to create just enough space. With the shot clock ticking down in the third quarter, Luka leaned back and launched a fadeaway three from 25 feet that splashed through, pushing LA's lead to 89-65. The Slovenian superstar stuffed the stat sheet on March 1, 2026 at Crypto.com Arena, posting 28 points, 9 assists, and going 4-8 from beyond the arc.

Athletes spend their lives refining their skills and craft but you’re either born with the magic or you’re not. Mere months into a mesmerizing career, Dallas Mavericks rookie Luka Dončić coordinates with teammate Jalen Brunson to cut hard into the corner with 0.6 seconds on the clock, catches a baseline inbound pass then lofts a high-arcing fallaway three into the net as he floats into the Portland Trail Blazers’ bench. Dončić’s three would knot the December 23, 2018 game at the end of regulation and while he wouldn’t claim this one, he would win Rookie of the Year honors, earn a spot on the All-Rookie First Team and pick up five Rookie of the Month nods along the way.

Two nights after his record-setting 60-point triple-double, Luka Dončić still had plenty of more reasons to celebrate. With just over a second remaining in the second quarter, the four-time Dallas Mavericks All-Star corralled a Spencer Dinwiddie inbounds pass and fired immediately from well beyond 30 feet to give his squad a 14-point halftime lead. Dončić’s sideline shimmy said it all, as his 35 points, 12 rebounds and 13 assists marked his eighth triple-double of the season and the fifth straight win for Dallas, a 129-114 decision over the Houston Rockets on December 29, 2022.

As the old basketball adage goes, a Game 7 is much easier when you have a player capable of being the best player on the floor. Seeking to stretch out a 30-point lead against the defending Western Conference champions, Dallas Mavericks star forward Luka Dončić took that to a different level, getting a pick-and-roll switch and using a between-the-legs dribble to put a Phoenix Suns defender on the floor before draining a three-pointer. Dončić was on a mission from the opening tip, outscoring the entire Suns team in the first half on the way to 35 points, 10 rebounds, six triples and four assists. This helped push the Mavericks to a 123-90 win in enemy territory and Dončić’s first-ever Western Conference Finals appearance on May 15, 2022.

Historic in his unique blend of creativity, dexterity, and confidence, Luka Dončić has the power to turn even the most hotly-contested battles into a personal game of “HORSE.” Completely unbothered after his initial fadeaway jumper gets blocked, the five-time All-Star finds time to retrieve the ball, lose it again, and then dagger the Houston Rockets’ hearts with a 1970s-esque rainbow hook shot to put the game out of reach. Leaving both himself and opponents with nothing to do but shrug, the Dallas Mavericks star constructed a Most Valuable Player-caliber performance, recording 41 points, nine rebounds, and nine assists, alongside a pair of steals and three 3-pointers, powering a clutch victory on November 28, 2023.

Having heard all of the chatter surrounding the foul trouble woes that plagued his chances of prevailing in the must-win Game Three, Luka Dončić, with a superstar-caliber response, determined that in Game Four of the 2024 NBA Finals, the foul moods would belong exclusively to the Boston Celtics. Resolute in making an impact on both ends of the floor, the reigning Western Conference Finals Most Valuable Player steps into action, barricading Jrue Holiday’s path to the rim on the way to an early-game steal. Knowingly settled into an efficient offensive groove, Dončić opts to turn it into a defense-to-offense series, overpowering the six-time All-Defensive Team selection on the low block before using a lightning-quick baseline spin to bank in a layup. With a brilliantly-timed performance, extending the Dallas Mavericks’ title hopes for another game, Dončić fittingly allowed himself a chance to sit and rest throughout the entire fourth quarter in the 38-point win on June 14, 2024. The performance on both ends spoke for itself as Dončić held opposing Celtics to just 2-of-11 shooting, while also recording 29 points —  25 in the first half —  along with five rebounds, five assists, and three steals in just 33 minutes of play.

When Luka Dončić walks into an NBA arena, his opponents know they’re in for a world of trouble. In this play, Dončić flexes his preternatural instincts for the game by driving one way, only to send a pinpoint dime behind his back and into the hands of his diving teammate at the bucket for the easy finish. Dončić erupted for a triple-double of 27 points, 13 boards and 10 dimes in the easy 112-85 victory over the Memphis Grizzlies on January 14, 2022.

When Luka Dončić gets his feet set for his signature fadeaway, you know it’s going in. On opening night, the new Lakers franchise player took control with the shot clock winding down. Here he drives left, gets to his spot and drains a cold-blooded stepback three-pointer from nearly 30 feet with the defenders hand in his face.

With one of the NBA’s smoothest handles, there are few defenses Dallas Mavericks star Luka Dončić can’t free himself of. With two Philadelphia 76ers to his left, Dončić shifts right with a quick between-the-legs move, creating a runway for a highlight flush in traffic. Dončić's box score told a similar story with 33 points, 13 rebounds, 15 assists and two steals in a 107-98 win on February 4, 2022.

Gifted with a shot-making ability that often goes both beyond comprehension and without an accurate superlative, it was of great irony that Luka Dončić stepped up to a big-time playoff moment with a patented stepback. Eye-to-eye with both his first chance at conquering the L.A. Clippers in the postseason and the player who famously made the stepback jumper his go-to method of excellence, Dončić freezes the moment in time, directing his teammates away, setting the stage for an isolation of the highest consequence. Finally prepared to offer James Harden a glimpse into the mirror with just six seconds left on the play clock, Dončić begins his motion, easing into a trusted spot atop the 3-point arc before sticking a 27-foot dagger, furnishing the Dallas Mavericks with a nine-point edge in the game’s final seconds. Extraordinary in one of the most complete two-way performances of his already-illustrious career, Dončić’s herculean efforts helped steer the Mavericks to a Game Two triumph and a 1-1 series tie. Engaged defensively enough to force opposing scorers into a 2-of-17 shooting performance as the primary defender, Dončić matched it with a predictably-superb offensive showing, erupting for 32 points, six rebounds, nine assists, one steal, one block, and five 3-pointers, prompting a memorable evening on April 23, 2024.

Punisher of the pick-and-roll by day; slayer of Western Conference No. 1 seeds by night. Crammed into a phone booth-tight situation with the Oklahoma City Thunder determined to neutralize his ball-screen brilliance with an aggressive blitz, Luka Dončić puts on a clinic on how to stay one step ahead, swinging a pass to his teammate before cutting into the wide-open space in the middle of the floor. Back in a reasonable situation with only Chet Holmgren blocking his path and his talented, lob-snatching teammate in his peripheral, Dončić turns to the tried-and-true connection, hanging an alley-oop pass through the skies for his teammate to snag on the way to a powerful two-handed flush. Two victories away from both returning to the Western Conference Finals and dethroning yet another top-ranked finisher in the Wild West, Dončić’s performance in the must-have Game Five reflected as such. Catapulting his team to victory on May 15, 2024, the five-time All-Star contributed 31 points, 10 rebounds, and 11 assists —  his second-consecutive triple-double and sixth of his postseason career — paired with one block and a game-high five 3-pointers.

When Dallas Mavericks superstar Luka Dončić gets his feet set for his signature fadeaway, you’d better be ready to catch it out of the net. Dončić gave the Boston Celtics dejà vu with two game-winners from the same spot in the same year. Here he drives left, gets to his spot and drains a cold-blooded stepback game-winning three-pointer with three opponents in his airspace. Dončić had 33 points, nine rebounds and five assists in a 107-104 victory on November 6, 2021.

If you’re gonna make a run at the Golden State Warriors, you’d better at least come equipped with a generational scorer capable of hitting any shot. Working off a drag screen near half court, Dallas Mavericks star guard Luka Dončić proves to be that guy, blowing by a defender on a pick-and-roll switch before hitting an off-balanced, high-arching leaner. Though ultimately for naught, Dončić’s efforts helped provide a small comeback scare. The All-Star finished his most successful season with 28 points, nine rebounds, six assists, three triples and one steal on May 26, 2022.

Peering up at a scoreboard that showed a red-hot Phoenix Suns team ahead by double-figures, Luka Dončić, through a magical feel for the game exclusive to almost only him, conducted a comeback attempt through a fireball of his own. Collecting a rebound on Josh Okogie’s misfired triple, Dončić coolly shifts his focus to a seemingly-mundane early-offense set with his new All-Star backcourt partner getting a step on Phoenix’s defense. In recognition of it upon even passing the Dallas Mavericks’ midcourt logo, Dončić, slingshotting a pass from behind his head, uncorks a perfectly-pinpoint cross-court dime, positioning a teammate for an extraordinary fastbreak bucket. Under Dončić’s overseeing, Dallas resiliently clawed back from a 13-point halftime deficit, ultimately falling one untimely foul shy of potentially overcoming the star-powered Suns on November 8, 2024. In elite form even so, the NBA’s reigning scoring champion constructed a 30-point showing (on 11-of-25) shooting, accompanied by seven rebounds, seven assists, one steal, and five 3-pointers in 42 minutes.

April 9, 2025’s spectacle against his former team might’ve began with heartfelt embraces and teardrops, but as is often the case with Luka Dončić, the forecast also called for 45-point rainstorms and almost-one-of-a-kind offense along the way. The recipe towards becoming just league history’s second-ever player to score 45+ for and against the same franchise in a single season was one that the Dallas Mavericks’ still-stunned crowd had come to know all too well over Dončić’s 472-game Texas reign. 3-point buckets — some built through immaculate footwork, others through mere spot-ups — crafty, almost “HORSE”-like shots around the rim, and ultimately, a final quarter takeover that vanquished any chance Dallas had of an upset. In what settled among 2024-25’s most-watched non-Christmas Day games, Dončić, through mixed emotions, treated fans of every allegiance to a 45-point, eight-rebound, six-assist, four-steal masterpiece in the Los Angeles Lakers’ victory. Paired with superb efficiency overall (16-of-28) and from downtown (7-of-10), Dončić again reaffirmed his status as a big-stage performer, eventually helping catapult L.A. to the No. 3 seed in the soon-arriving 2025 NBA Playoffs.

With an individual bar already set higher than nearly any 24-year-old in the NBA’s existence, Luka Dončić would’ve been reasonably defended from criticism, should 2022-23’s historic pace have been difficult to replicate. Instead, through his trademark array of stepbacks, pivots, and nifty footwork, the Dallas Mavericks superstar concluded 2023-24 with nearly every hurdle cleared. Familiar enough with the term “historic” to call it a relative, Dončić again made pleasantries, registering a first-of-its-kind statline that read as follows: 33.9 points, 9.2 rebounds, 9.8 assists, and 1.4 steals per game. Through refined touch, the already-unguardable All-Star also raised his percentages from the 3-point line (38.2) and charity stripe (78.6) to career-bests. A nightly threat to turn a must-win game into a personal trick-shot extravaganza, Dončić, donning a signature smile and a third-place Most Valuable Player finish to show for his efforts, produced a season that aged like wine. From the four-triples-in-three-minutes takeover against Brooklyn to the 73-point masterpiece in Atlanta — fourth-most in league history — to his warrior-like trek to the 2024 NBA Finals, Dončić’s season left behind only one nightmarish question for opposing defenders to contemplate: No. 77 can’t possibly get even better, can he?

The list of players capable of evoking cheers and “M-V-P” chants from a road arena isn’t an abundant one, but six years into his breathtaking career, Luka Dončić has proven there’s no list he’s incapable of getting on. Fierce in sending the Atlanta Hawks a message from the opening position, the four-time All-NBA selection punished the opposition with pull-ups, pivots, hard-earned lessons for the seven defenders who attempted to guard him, and perhaps most importantly, very few misses along the way. Dončić’s trademark calm, controlled style of play worked in perfect conflict with his box score, as the Dallas Mavericks superstar eased his way into the fourth-most points in NBA history, as well as the Association’s most efficient 70-point performance. In proving to be a handful for Atlanta during the win on January 26, 2024, Dončić’s full box score was a mouthful, reading as follows: 73 points (on 25 of 33 shooting), 10 rebounds, seven assists, one steal, and eight 3-pointers, putting him on the single-game scoring Mount Rushmore.

You could write a textbook about how Luka Doncic uses angles and momentum to manipulate the defense. The 21-year-old rocks world-class Houston Rockets defender P.J. Tucker onto his heels before claiming his space in the paint and dishing off to Willie Cauley-Stein for an alley-oop.

Just because Luka Dončić has mastered the finesse game doesn’t mean he won’t still flush one in the paint. The Dallas Mavericks guard finds a gap in the defense then attacks it for a thundering slam in the NBA All-Star Game on March 7, 2021.
Dallas Mavericks breakout star Luka Dončić brings the ball up the court, splits the defense, and drives to the rack for the ferocious one-handed slam against the Denver Nuggets on March 11, 2020.

Oh, Luka! Dallas Mavericks superstar guard Luka Dončić nails the clutch stepback three pointer to win game 4 of their opening round matchup against the LA Clippers and tie the series at two games apiece on August 23, 2020.

Luka Doncic has never found a passing lane he couldn’t hit. The Dallas Mavericks superstar weaves through a pair of Chicago Bulls defenders before hitting teammate Willie Cauley-Stein with a perfectly placed behind-the-back pass at the hoop on January 17, 2021.

Luka with the superb finger roll! Luka Dončić of the Dallas Mavericks drives hard to the rim and drops the sweet layup off the glass against the Los Angeles Lakers on December 25, 2020. Dončić was his usual sensational self in the Christmas Day matchup, notching 27 points, 7 assists, and 4 rebounds.

Cut to the hoop and let Luka Dončić take care of the rest. The Dallas Mavericks superstar dumps a pass behind the back of Phoenix Suns defender Deandre Ayton to a streaking Dorian Finney-Smith in an opening night battle on December 23, 2020.

Vision won’t get you far if you can’t get your man the rock. Dallas Mavericks guard Luka Doncic watches Kristaps Porzingis roll perfectly out of a screen, then reaches way out around his defender to fire a sidewinding bullet pass to the wide-open center in the paint on January 20, 2021. Doncic walked away with a cool 13-point, 12-rebound, 12-assist triple double in the win.
